groups.heading: config: hosts was REJECTED, now ACCEPTED

answers.why: Probe shows config hosts=['2459::52d2%lo0'] is rejected by the zod 3 oracle and accepted by the merged build, so this is a real verdict change in the looser direction; the accepted value is stored unchanged (the array round-trips as given). The important part: review/corpus-diffs.md signs off KEEP OLD for zoned IPv6 and claims the union 'reproduces exactly the set zod 3 matched ... nothing *new* is let in'. A probe contradicts that: zod 3's .ip() accepted 'fe80::1%eth0' but REJECTED zoned non-fe80 addresses, while the merged zonedIpv6 refine accepts a %zone on any address that z.ipv6() likes (fe80=A/A, global=R/A). So the 508 diffs here are not the signed-off restoration; they are a widening beyond both zod 3 and zod 4. Judgement: a human must act - this is 5% of the fuzz corpus and hosts feeds connection targets, and accepting a zone index on a global/ULA address is almost certainly not what the reviewer intended to approve. Judgement on real_clients: yes - the widened set includes plainly legitimate link-local forms that zod 3 happened to reject (e.g. uppercase 'FE80::1%eth0', see the signup probe in the ip group), so well-behaved callers do live in this newly-accepted region.

claims.claim: config.hosts with a zoned IPv6 address that is not fe80:: is rejected by zod 3 and accepted by the merged build (verdict change, looser).

The merged zoned-IPv6 branch is wider than zod 3's .ip(): zod 3 accepted the zone suffix on 'fe80::1%eth0' but not on other IPv6 addresses, so these acceptances are new behaviour, not restored zod 3 behaviour.

groups.heading: config: timeoutMs was ACCEPTED, now REJECTED

answers.why: Probe: timeoutMs=Infinity is accepted by the zod 3 oracle and stored as Infinity, and is rejected by the merged build ('Invalid input: expected number, received Infinity'); zod 4's z.number() excludes non-finite values. That is a verdict change, stricter. No input is accepted by both with a different stored value here. review/corpus-diffs.md covers only ip, name, age and a list of silent API moves - it never mentions timeoutMs or finiteness - so this specific change was not signed off (fact: I read the whole file). Judgement on real_clients: no - Infinity is not expressible as a JSON literal; it only arises from numeric overflow (JSON.parse('1e999') === Infinity, probed) or from an explicit Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY, and finite values including 1e308 still pass. An infinite timeout was nonsense under zod 3 too (it was stored and would have disabled the timeout silently), so zod 4 fails closed on something that was already a latent bug. Judgement: low risk, but worth one line in the PR description because a deployment that currently boots with an overflowed timeoutMs would now fail at config load.

claims.claim: timeoutMs=Infinity is accepted by zod 3 (stored as Infinity) and rejected by the merged build.
Infinity is only reachable through numeric overflow in JSON, and ordinary large finite timeouts are still accepted by the merged build.

groups.heading: signup: ip was REJECTED, now ACCEPTED

answers.why: Same root cause as the hosts group, on the signup.ip field (both use the shared ipAddress union in src/schemas.ts). Probe: zod 3 accepts 'fe80::1%eth0' and so does the merged build (that part is the signed-off restoration), but zod 3 REJECTS 'FE80::1%eth0', '2001:db8::1%eth0' and '::%1' while the merged build accepts all three. So the 357 diffs are a widening past zod 3, not a restoration of it, and review/corpus-diffs.md's sign-off text explicitly asserts the opposite ('nothing *new* is let in'); a claim that is factually wrong cannot count as sign-off for this behaviour. The accepted string is stored verbatim, so no stored-value issue. Judgement on real_clients: yes - uppercase hex link-local addresses and fully-expanded fe80 addresses are perfectly well-formed input that a real client sends, and they fall inside the newly accepted region. Judgement: a human must decide whether to tighten zonedIpv6 to the link-local prefix (or accept the wider set deliberately), because ip is used for abuse/geo decisions downstream.

claims.claim: signup.ip: the signed-off case 'fe80::1%eth0' is accepted by both versions, but uppercase link-local, documentation-prefix and unspecified zoned addresses are rejected by zod 3 and accepted by the merged build.
A newly accepted zoned address is stored verbatim (no normalisation), so the only change is the verdict.

groups.heading: signup: age was ACCEPTED, now REJECTED

answers.why: Probe reproduces the group exactly: age=9007199254740994 and age=1e21 are accepted by zod 3 and rejected by the merged build with 'Too big: expected int to be <=9007199254740991' (zod 4's .int() means safe integer), while a normal age (42) is accepted by both. review/corpus-diffs.md section '[2] age - was ACCEPTED, now REJECTED' describes this exact change (same values 1e+21 and 9007199254740992), recommends ACCEPT NEW with no code change, and lists it in the sign-off block - so this is the same change a human already reviewed; the fuzzer simply generates far more of these values than the 400-request corpus contained. Judgement on real_clients: no - every example is above 2^53 where the float grid is coarser than 1; none of them is an age, and the reviewer reached the same conclusion. Judgement: no new action beyond the follow-up already noted in the doc (give age a real .max()).

claims.claim: Unsafe-integer ages are accepted by zod 3 and rejected by the merged build, with the zod 4 safe-integer message.
Ordinary ages are unaffected: 42 is accepted by both versions, so the tightening is confined to values past 2^53.

groups.heading: signup: rejected by both, but different fields reported

answers.why: Every example in this group is rejected by both versions, and my probes confirm it (bothReject=true in both reconstructions), so no input flips verdict and nothing is stored. The field-set deltas are entirely the shadow of two other groups: 'ip' disappears from the list when the input carries a zoned IPv6 address (the signup ip group, looser), and 'age' appears when the input carries an unsafe integer (the age group, stricter) - probed both directions. review/corpus-diffs.md does not discuss which fields are reported on already-invalid inputs (it notes only that the corpus comparison ignores message wording), so I record already_signed_off=false for this group itself; the age half of the cause is signed off, the ip half is not. Judgement on real_clients: no - these payloads are invalid under both versions, so no well-behaved client depends on them; the only consumer impact is the content of the 400 response body. Judgement: as a group this needs no separate action - fixing the ip group removes the ip half automatically - but it should not be read as independent evidence of safety.

claims.claim: An invalid signup carrying a zoned IPv6 address is rejected by both versions, but the merged build no longer reports the ip field.
An invalid signup carrying an unsafe-integer age is rejected by both versions, but the merged build additionally reports the age field.

groups.heading: config: rejected by both, but different fields reported

answers.why: Same shape as the signup version: probe reconstructs one of the listed examples ({hosts:['2459::52d2%lo0','bad'], timeoutMs:Infinity}) and both versions reject it (bothReject=true), with zod 3 reporting hosts.0,hosts.1 and the merged build reporting hosts.1,timeoutMs. So no verdict flips and nothing is stored; the deltas are the hosts widening (hosts group) removing a hosts.N entry and the Infinity tightening (timeoutMs group) adding a timeoutMs entry. Not discussed in review/corpus-diffs.md, hence already_signed_off=false. Judgement on real_clients: no - every input here is invalid under both versions. Judgement: no independent action; it resolves when the hosts and timeoutMs groups are settled.

claims.claim: A config with a zoned host, a junk host and timeoutMs=Infinity is rejected by both versions but reports different fields (hosts.0 drops out, timeoutMs appears).

groups.heading: signup: website accepted, but the PARSED VALUE changed

answers.why: Probe: ' https://example.com' and 'https://example.com/a?b=c ' are accepted by BOTH versions, but zod 3 stores the string verbatim (with the surrounding whitespace) while zod 4's z.url() stores the trimmed value; a clean URL is stored identically by both, so the change is confined to whitespace-padded input. No verdict flips in this group. review/corpus-diffs.md lists z.string().url() -> z.url() under 'Silent API moves (no corpus difference)' and asserts it produced identical answers on all 400 requests - it therefore does not sign off a stored-value change, it denies one exists; the 400-request corpus simply contained no padded URL. Judgement on real_clients: yes - a leading space or trailing newline on a pasted URL from a web form is very ordinary input. Judgement: a human should confirm this is wanted (it is arguably an improvement - the stored column gets a clean URL), but it changes persisted data and any downstream exact-string comparison or dedup against previously stored values, so it should be an explicit decision rather than an inherited one.

claims.claim: A whitespace-padded website URL is accepted by both versions but stored with the padding by zod 3 and trimmed by the merged build.
A clean URL is stored identically by both versions, so the merged build is not rewriting URLs in general - only trimming surrounding whitespace.
